details: CONFIRMED by reading the loops (relay_verdict._merge_findings line 681 loops over every merge; relay_inert.resolved per
merge; relay_marks.get per candidate commit) and by the probe breakdown below. Memoisation removes repeats, not per-item
calls; batching (one `rev-list --parents`, one `diff-tree --stdin -m --name-only` for all merges, one `cat-file --batch`
for the stored marks and trees) is what makes the count flat, as the brief's What line suggested.
Whether 78 is "small" is the owner's call; growth with merges is not.
Size: 60 agent minutes (batching two loops plus a scaling test), or 5 if the owner accepts the current target.
evidence: python3 -I probe_count.py <wt>/tests out.log   (runs CheckerStop.train_ready + relay_record with the test's own spy)
failing_case: The brief's pass case: "One relay check run starts a small fixed number of git processes ... independent of the number of
records". The fix keeps answers so no question is asked twice, but each distinct merge, commit and stored mark is still its
own process: per merge in _merge_findings (rev-parse --verify -q <m>^2, merge-base --is-ancestor, diff <m>^1 <m>), per merge
in relay_inert.resolved/dropped (3 rev-parse, merge-tree, diff), per commit tree (ls-tree -r -z <sha>, 8 in one run), per
stored mark (show <sha>:.relay/checks/<c>.json). One record on the test's train of three merges: 78 processes, of them
8 ls-tree -r, 8 rev-parse --verify <sha>^{commit}, 8 diff --name-only. A train with ten merges and ten marks starts more,
and the test (ceiling 120 on one fixture, its own comment: "not a per-record bound") passes either way.
The hook part of the brief ("Same for the hook that runs it") got only the process-wide sha cache: no count, no test.
fix_hint: Batch the per-merge reads of _merge_findings and relay_inert.resolved into one rev-list --parents plus one
diff-tree --stdin call, and read stored marks with one cat-file --batch; add a test that grows the fixture by k merges and
asserts the count does not grow. If that is judged too large, ask the owner to set the target in the item's notes.
pass_cases: 1. The train fixture of test_one_check_record_..., record run counted: N processes. The same fixture with three more merges of
the default branch and two more stored marks: the count is still N (or N + a fixed constant stated in the test), not
2. No distinct question asked twice in one record run (the existing assertion) keeps passing.
3. The check-mark hook run on one check data file starts at most a stated number of git processes, asserted by a spy test.
4. Or, if the owner sets the target at "about 80 and growing with merges": the item's notes record that word and the
brief's pass case is amended; then this finding is closed by that decision.
reason: tests/test_check_mark_hook.py:222 (record count flat with extra merges/marks) and :246 (hook).
findings.summary: a check run still starts git processes per merge, per commit tree and per stored mark; the brief's 'independent of the number of records' is not met or tested

details: CONFIRMED by a python probe (evidence). `_is_pure` skips every argument that starts with "-" and counts only revision
arguments, so `diff` with one revision (which compares against the working tree) and options that pull in refs (--all,
--branches, --tags, --glob, --remotes, --cached, --stdin) pass as pure. LOW: correct for every current caller, fragile.
evidence: python3 -I -c "... relay_git.git(r,'diff','--name-only',sha) ... edit f ... again ... subprocess git diff"
failing_case: In one process: relay_git.git(repo, "diff", "--name-only", <full sha of HEAD>) returns '' ; edit a tracked file; the same
call returns '' again (kept), while git itself answers 'f'. Same class: rev-list --all <sha>, diff --cached <sha>,
diff <sha> -- path. No relay caller asks these through relay_git today (relay_precheck asks `diff --name-only <base>` through
its own subprocess), so nothing is wrong yet; the first caller that moves to relay_git gets stale answers silently.
fix_hint: In _is_pure: for `diff` require two revisions or one a..b; return False on any of --all, --branches, --tags, --remotes,
pass_cases: 1. diff --name-only <sha>, then a worktree edit, then the same call: the second answer lists the edited file.
2. diff --name-only <sha1> <sha2> asked twice starts one process (kept, as now).
3. diff --name-only <sha1>..<sha2> asked twice starts one process (kept, as now).
4. rev-list --all <sha> asked twice starts two processes.
5. rev-list --count <sha> asked twice starts one process (test_a_question_about_a_full_sha_is_asked_once keeps passing).
reason: GitAnswersKept one-revision diff and shape-of-question tests pass and fail on the old code.
findings.summary: the process-wide cache treats a one-revision `git diff <sha>` (worktree compare) and ref options like --all as never changing
